questions.question: What is the inner product ⟨a,b⟩ of two length-n vectors over a field?
options: The element-wise sum a₁+b₁, …, aₙ+bₙ
The sum of products a₁·b₁ + … + aₙ·bₙ
The product of sums (a₁+…+aₙ)·(b₁+…+bₙ)
The maximum coordinate of a minus the maximum coordinate of b
questions.explanation: By definition, ⟨a,b⟩ = Σᵢ aᵢ·bᵢ (computed in the field).

questions.question: In Fiat–Shamir transforms, why do we hash the transcript to get a challenge?
options: To reduce the proof size to exactly 1 group element
To make verifier randomness deterministic from public data
To let the prover pick challenges that minimize proof size
To avoid computing inverses in the finite field
questions.explanation: Fiat–Shamir replaces interactive verifier randomness with a hash of what the verifier has seen so far.

questions.question: What statement does the IPA verifier ultimately want to be true (in this lesson’s notation)?
options: P' = a·G + b·H, where a and b are scalars (not vectors)
P' = ⟨a,G⟩ + ⟨b,H⟩, without any Q term
questions.explanation: The extra Q term binds the inner product ⟨a,b⟩ into the same equation as the vector commitment.

questions.question: If n is a power of two, how many IPA rounds does the prover send (L,R) pairs?
options: n rounds
n/2 rounds
log₂(n) rounds
1 round (independent of n)
questions.explanation: Each round halves the vector length, so it takes log₂(n) folds to reach length 1.

questions.question: Why must the per-round challenge u be nonzero in an IPA?
options: Because u is used only as u², and 0² would be undefined
Because the protocol needs u⁻¹ to fold vectors and generators
Because u must be a primitive root of the field modulus
Because u must equal the inner product ⟨a,b⟩
questions.explanation: Folding uses both u and u⁻¹; if u=0 then u⁻¹ does not exist and the protocol breaks.

questions.question: Which transcript elements must be hashed (directly or indirectly) to prevent replaying the same proof under a different statement?
options: Only the final scalars a and b
Only L and R values, not the public statement
The public statement (P',G,H,Q) and the per-round messages (L,R)
Only the vector length n and the field modulus p
questions.explanation: If the public statement is not bound into the transcript, the same L,R sequence could be reused across different statements.

questions.question: Attack intuition: what breaks if the prover can choose challenges u after seeing what would make verification pass?
options: Nothing breaks; u is only a performance parameter
Soundness can break because u controls the folding equations
Completeness breaks because honest proofs cannot be generated
Zero-knowledge breaks because L and R become constant
questions.explanation: Challenges must be unpredictable to the prover; otherwise they can try to steer the fold to satisfy the final check without a real witness.

questions.question: Why is the toy group in this lesson (integers mod p under addition) not a faithful security model of real IPA deployments?
options: Because it has no modular arithmetic at all
Because discrete log relations between generators are trivial in Z_p
Because elliptic curves cannot represent vectors of generators
Because Fiat–Shamir hashing is impossible over integers
questions.explanation: In Z_p, any nonzero element is a known multiple of any other; real deployments rely on unknown discrete log relations in curve groups.
